questions.scenario: Resource group RG1 contains a storage account named st1 and a virtual network named VNet1. You deploy a template to RG1 that defines only st1. You do not specify a deployment mode.
questions.question: What happens to VNet1?

options.why: Correct. The default mode is Incremental, which leaves resources that are not in the template alone.
Resources are deleted only in Complete mode.

options.text: VNet1 is moved to a new resource group
options.why: Deployments do not move resources.

options.text: The deployment fails because VNet1 is not in the template
options.why: Incremental deployments succeed even when other resources exist in the group.

questions.explanation: Incremental is the default mode. Complete mode deletes resources that are not defined in the template.

questions.question: You need to review the resources that a Bicep deployment will create, modify, or delete in resource group RG1 without making any changes. Which command should you run?

options.text: az deployment group what-if --resource-group RG1 --template-file main.bicep
options.why: Correct. what-if previews create, modify, and delete operations without deploying.

options.text: az deployment group create --resource-group RG1 --template-file main.bicep --mode Complete
options.why: This deploys the template and can delete resources.
This compiles the file to JSON but does not compare it with the resource group.
This exports the current resources and does not preview the template.

questions.explanation: In PowerShell, use New-AzResourceGroupDeployment with the -WhatIf parameter.

questions.scenario: Several resources in RG1 were created manually in the Azure portal. You must create a template that represents the current state of RG1 with the least administrative effort.
questions.question: What should you use?

options.why: Correct. Export template generates a template from the existing resources in the group.
Deployment history contains only resources that were deployed with templates, not portal-created resources outside deployments.
Decompile converts an existing JSON file. It does not read resources from Azure.
A template spec stores a template you already have.

questions.explanation: Export template (or az group export) captures current resources. Review it, because names and values are hard-coded and some properties cannot be exported.

questions.question: You have an ARM template named azuredeploy.json. You need to convert it to a Bicep file. Which command should you run?

options.why: Correct. decompile converts ARM JSON to Bicep.
build compiles a Bicep file to JSON, which is the opposite direction.
deployment group export downloads the template of a past deployment and does not convert files.
format tidies the layout of a Bicep file.

questions.explanation: Decompilation is best effort. Review warnings and refactor the generated Bicep before you use it.

questions.scenario: You must deploy a Bicep file named main.bicep to resource group RG1. Any resources in RG1 that are not defined in main.bicep must be removed.
questions.question: Which two commands meet the requirement? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: az deployment group create --resource-group RG1 --template-file main.bicep --mode Complete
options.why: Correct. Complete mode removes resources that are not defined in the template.
Correct. This is the PowerShell equivalent with Complete mode.

options.text: az deployment group create --resource-group RG1 --template-file main.bicep
options.why: Without --mode the deployment is Incremental and does not remove other resources.

options.text: az deployment group what-if --resource-group RG1 --template-file main.bicep --mode Complete
options.why: what-if only previews the changes. Nothing is removed.

questions.explanation: Run what-if before a Complete-mode deployment to see which resources will be deleted.
